**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: three hours.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will be penalised.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorised composition will be severely sanctioned.

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** Use any three non-Cameroonian prescribed texts to show their relevance to the Cameroonian society.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Corrige de methode (the prescribed texts are not available for this model answer)**

**What the question asks.** Choose THREE prescribed texts written by non-Cameroonian authors, and for each show that its themes or characters speak to life in Cameroon today. The answer is a short essay, not a list of plots.

**Plan (20 marks, no breakdown printed)**

1. **Introduction** (3 to 4 lines): say what "relevance" means (a theme, a problem or a human type that Cameroonians recognise in their own society) and name the three texts you will use.
2. **Body, one paragraph per text** (the same four steps each time):
   - the text, its writer and the theme you pick;
   - one precise example from the text (a character, an event or a scene you remember well);
   - the Cameroonian reality it matches (for instance: poverty and unemployment, corruption and abuse of power, the position of women, the clash between tradition and modernity, family and generational conflict, the colonial heritage, the rural exodus);
   - a short comment: what the Cameroonian reader can learn.
3. **Conclusion** (2 to 3 lines): the common point of the three texts and the general lesson for Cameroonian society.

**Marking.** Credit goes to the choice of three genuinely non-Cameroonian texts, accurate and specific examples, a clear link with Cameroon for each one, and organised, correct English. **Common mistakes:** using a Cameroonian text; telling the story without the link to Cameroon; treating only one or two texts.
